transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get the stability sprint planning underway. As a reminder, we've got a ten-business-day sprint with capacity for one primary technical-debt focus, and the three candidates on the table are legacy_csv_exporter, webhook_retry_service, and admin_search_index. Before I lock the plan, I want to do our usual round-robin check-in. I'd like to hear from backend engineering, security engineering, and customer support — please share your perspective on which of these three items you think should be the priority and why. I'll make the final call once I've heard from all three.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While finishing an unrelated export ticket this afternoon, I confirmed that legacy_csv_exporter already has six of its eight endpoint migrations completed. Exactly two endpoints remain, and the backend team can finish those two within this sprint. I haven't updated the planning board yet, but this means legacy_csv_exporter is very close to done and could be fully completed during this sprint.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a security finding before we go further. Minutes ago I confirmed in the dependency scanner that legacy_csv_exporter still packages libxml 3.9.4, which has a known exploitable parsing vulnerability. The approved remediation target is exactly libxml 4.1.0. I was verifying scanner results and hadn't filed the finding yet, but given Devon just told us legacy_csv_exporter is close to completion and could be finished this sprint, I think this has to factor heavily into the decision. Upgrading that dependency should be part of any work on legacy_csv_exporter, and doing both the endpoint migrations and the libxml upgrade together this sprint would close out a real security risk.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have something important to add from the customer support side. During a customer call this morning, I confirmed that exactly 42 enterprise accounts still depend on legacy_csv_exporter's old audit-column behavior. Those accounts need a migration guide before the new behavior is enabled. I recorded the call in a support note that hasn't synced to the sprint-planning system yet, so this wouldn't be visible to anyone looking at the board. If we prioritize legacy_csv_exporter this sprint — especially if we're completing the remaining endpoint migrations and upgrading the libxml dependency — we need to account for the migration guide work for those 42 accounts, or we risk breaking audit workflows for a significant number of enterprise customers.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Complete the remaining two endpoint migrations for legacy_csv_exporter within the ten-business-day sprint.
Upgrade libxml from 3.9.4 to the approved remediation target 4.1.0 as part of the legacy_csv_exporter work this sprint.
Produce and deliver a migration guide for the 42 enterprise accounts that depend on the old audit-column behavior before the new behavior is enabled.
